messages.content: Audit our vendored dependency manifest for license risk before the acquisition due-diligence call. Flag anything copyleft that could taint commercial redistribution.
Manifest loaded — 312 packages resolved from the internal registry. Running the license policy scan rather than eyeballing each entry.

messages.name: run_command
messages.content:
license scan: 312 packages checked against policy 'commercial-redistribution'
  ALLOW  309 packages (MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD / ISC / MPL-2.0)
  FLAG   libfoo-native 2.4.1  GPL-3.0-only   (native addon, statically linked)
  FLAG   pdf-render 1.9.0     AGPL-3.0       (network-service copyleft)
  FLAG   geo-tiles 0.8.2      GPL-2.0+       (bundled at build time)
policy notes: static linking extends GPL obligations to the linking binary; AGPL triggers on network use alone.

Three copyleft findings out of 312 packages: libfoo-native 2.4.1 (GPL-3.0-only, statically linked native addon — obligations extend to our binary), pdf-render 1.9.0 (AGPL-3.0 — copyleft triggers on network use, which is exactly how we deploy), and geo-tiles 0.8.2 (GPL-2.0+, bundled at build time). Everything else is permissive (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/ISC) or file-scoped MPL-2.0.
Of those three, which one blocks commercial redistribution outright as we ship today, and what replacement approach do you suggest for each?
